questions.stem: Choose the pair which is closest to the similar in meaning
questions.explanation: Lawsuit and litigation both mean the process of taking a dispute to court. The other pairs are related or opposed, not similar.

questions.stem: Choose the pair which is closest to the similar in meaning
questions.explanation: Libelous (written) and slanderous (spoken) both mean defamatory. Guilty/innocent and prosecutor/defense are opposites.

questions.stem: Choose the pair which is closest to the similar in meaning
questions.explanation: Mitigating and extenuating both describe circumstances that reduce the seriousness of an offence.

questions.stem: Choose the pair which is closest to the similar in meaning
questions.explanation: Damages (money awarded by a court) means compensation. Liability and immunity are opposites; negligence is the opposite of cautious.

questions.stem: Choose the pair which is closest to the similar in meaning
questions.explanation: A testament is a will. Beneficiary (receives) and executor (administers) are different roles.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence: A person who speaks many languages fluently
questions.explanation: Polyglot = one who speaks many languages. A linguist studies language; a translator converts text.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence: A person who deliberately sets fire to property
questions.explanation: Arsonist = one who deliberately sets fire to property. A pyromaniac has an irresistible urge to start fires.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence: The philosophical study of the nature of being, reality and existence
questions.explanation: Ontology is the study of being and existence. Epistemology is the study of knowledge. (Metaphysics is the wider branch, but the key is ontology.)

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence: A speech in which a person talks to themselves, often used in drama
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is a speech made alone on stage. A monologue is addressed to others.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence: The process by which something, especially a word or phrase, is adapted into a new cultural or social context
questions.explanation: Assimilation is absorbing and adapting something into a new cultural setting. Treat this one as medium-ambiguous; the key is A.

questions.stem: Identify that part of the given sentence which is not acceptable in standard written English: The new employee, who's name is John, is very friendly.
questions.explanation: 'Who's' means 'who is'. The possessive is 'whose'.

questions.stem: Identify that part of the given sentence which is not acceptable in standard written English: The new policy will effect all employees starting next month.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' (verb) = influence. 'Effect' as a verb means to bring about.

questions.stem: Identify that part of the given sentence which is not acceptable in standard written English: The new employee is very friendly and helpful, but he dont know much about the company.
options: dont know much about the company
questions.explanation: Should be 'doesn't know'. With 'he' the auxiliary is 'does'.

questions.stem: Identify that part of the given sentence which is not acceptable in standard written English: The company will hire hundreds of new employees in the next few month.
questions.explanation: 'A few' / 'few' takes a plural noun: 'months'.

questions.stem: Identify that part of the given sentence which is not acceptable in standard written English: I feel so week after running a marathon, but I will be back to my normal self by next day.
options: but I will be back to
my normal self by next day
questions.explanation: 'Week' (7 days) is wrongly used for 'weak' (lacking strength).

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: She decided to 'bite the bullet' and start her own business despite the risks.
questions.explanation: To bite the bullet = to face something unpleasant or difficult with courage.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: He tried to 'throw his weight around' to get the team to follow his orders.
options: Use influence or authority in an overbearing way
questions.explanation: To throw one's weight around = to use power or authority in a bossy way.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: The manager's promises turned out to be a 'red herring'.
options: A deliberate distraction from the main issue
questions.explanation: A red herring is a misleading clue or distraction.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: He was determined to 'hit the ground running' on the new project.
options: Start something with enthusiasm and energy
Take a slow and cautious approach
questions.explanation: Hit the ground running = start a task quickly and effectively.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: The plan worked, but it was a 'Pyrrhic victory' for the company.
options: A loss disguised as a win
A victory achieved at great cost, almost to the point of being a loss
questions.explanation: Named after King Pyrrhus, whose victories cost him most of his army.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: The government is determined to put an end to the illegal practices that have been going on ____ the radar and bring the perpetrators to ____.
questions.explanation: 'Under the radar' (unnoticed) and 'bring to justice' are the standard collocations.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: The witness's statement added ____ to the investigation and ultimately helped to ____ the mystery surrounding the case.
questions.explanation: A helpful statement adds clarity and helps solve a mystery.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: When the storm hit, the people took ____ in the shelters and waited for the situation to ____.
questions.explanation: 'Took refuge' and 'subside' fit. 'Took shelter in the shelters' repeats the word awkwardly.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: The scientist's groundbreaking discovery opened ____ to new possibilities and set ____ for further research.
questions.explanation: 'Opened doors' and 'set trends' are the natural collocations.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: Despite being criticized, the athlete managed to keep her ____ held high and rose ____ the occasion in the final match.
questions.explanation: 'Keep one's head held high' and 'rise to the occasion'.

questions.stem: Choose the paragraph which has the most logical order of sentences. (1) The new policy was implemented to reduce traffic congestion. (2) The policy restricted traffic in the city center during peak hours. (3) The number of accidents de-escalated after the policy was implemented.
questions.explanation: Purpose first (1), then what the policy did (2), then the result (3).

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: French people love cooking, ____ the English don't seem very interested.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two facts.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: A ____ is a unit of sound.
questions.explanation: A syllable is a unit of pronunciation containing one vowel sound.

questions.stem: Select the most appropriate meaning of the word: TRUCE
questions.explanation: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting for a time.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: At one point, it looked as if an area of agreement would ____, especially over the issue of productivity-linked wages.
questions.explanation: 'Emerge' is intransitive and fits 'an area of agreement would emerge'. 'Create' needs an object.

questions.stem: Select the word with the incorrect spelling.
questions.explanation: Correct spelling: unpretentious.

questions.stem: Select the word with the incorrect spelling.
questions.explanation: Correct spelling: pedestrian.

questions.stem: Select the word with the incorrect spelling.
questions.explanation: Correct spelling: innocuous (double n).

questions.stem: Choose the correct antonym of the word 'generosity'.
questions.explanation: Altruism and largesse are synonyms of generosity. Of the options, malevolence (ill will) is the opposite.

questions.stem: Choose the antonym of the word 'analogue'.
questions.explanation: An analogue is something similar or parallel. 'Difference' is the opposite of similarity. (The sheet shows a candidate chose 'correlate', which is a synonym.)

questions.stem: Choose the antonym of 'amusement'.
questions.explanation: Amusement = enjoyment; melancholy = sadness.

questions.stem: Choose the word which is correctly spelt:
questions.explanation: Exonerate = to clear of blame.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'to take someone for a ride':
options: to give a ride to someone
questions.explanation: To take someone for a ride = to cheat or trick them.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'to move heaven and earth':
questions.explanation: To move heaven and earth = to make every possible effort.

questions.stem: Give a single word for 'One who eats everything'.
questions.explanation: Omnivorous = eating all kinds of food. Omniscient = all-knowing; omnipresent = everywhere; omnipotent = all-powerful.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which gives the best meaning of the word 'compensate':
questions.explanation: Compensate = to make up for a loss or harm.

questions.stem: Identify the sentence with correct punctuation:
questions.explanation: No comma is needed inside this simple sentence.

questions.stem:
Passage: Mohan works in a restaurant in the centre of New Delhi. He goes to work at 5pm, but yesterday at 5pm, he wasn't on the bus, he was in a taxi going to the hospital. He was very sick! Usually, he works in the kitchen all evening, but yesterday he wasn't in the kitchen. He was in the X-ray department of the hospital because the doctors were worried about his stomach pains. Normally, at 11pm, Mohan takes a bus to go home after finishing at the restaurant, but yesterday at 11pm, he was still in the hospital and he was still unhappy and sick. He was in a bed and he was very hot - 102 degrees! Was he worried? Yes, he was! In the morning, he was better and the doctors were pleased. What was the problem? It was bad food - from his restaurant!

Statement: Mohan was in the restaurant yesterday afternoon.
questions.explanation: At 5pm he was in a taxi going to hospital, so he wasn't at the restaurant.

questions.explanation: 'Usually' he takes the bus; yesterday was the exception.

questions.stem: What comes next in the series in place of ? : X, T, P, L, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves back 4 places (X=24, T=20, P=16, L=12), so the next is 8 = H.

questions.stem:
Statements: All dogs are animals. Some animals are cats.
Conclusion 1: Some dogs are cats.
Conclusion 2: Some animals are dogs.
questions.explanation: All dogs are animals, so some animals are dogs (conversion). Nothing links dogs to cats.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Tennis : Racket :: Cricket : ?
questions.explanation: The racket is the equipment used to hit the ball in tennis; the bat does this in cricket.

questions.stem: How many meaningful words can you form from the letters 'LEAP'?
questions.explanation: LEAP, PALE, PEAL and PLEA make four. (Candidates who picked 3 missed one.)

questions.stem: Aman starts walking 10 m east, then turns left and walks 5 m. He turns left again and walks 10 m. He turns left again and goes 10 m. In which direction is he now facing?
questions.explanation: East, then left = North, left = West, left = South. He is facing South.

questions.stem: X says, "Y is my mother's only daughter." How is Y related to X?
questions.explanation: The mother's only daughter, from X's point of view, is X's sister.

questions.stem: In a family of six members, A is married to B. C is B's sister, and D is C's father. F is D's mother. How is F related to A?
questions.explanation: D is B's father, so F (D's mother) is B's grandmother, which makes her A's grandmother-in-law.

questions.stem: In a certain code, ROAD is written as URDG. How is FAST written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 3: F-I, A-D, S-V, T-W gives IDVW.

questions.stem: If in a certain language NATURE is coded as MASUQE, how is FAMINE coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters 1, 3, 5 move back 1; letters 2, 4, 6 stay. F-E, A-A, M-L, I-I, N-M, E-E gives EALIME.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Flow : River :: Stagnant : ?
questions.explanation: A river flows; a pool is stagnant water.

questions.stem: How will the word 'FLOWER' appear in the mirror?
questions.explanation: A lateral mirror reverses the order of letters (each also flipped). The letters in reverse order are REWOLF.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Peacock : India :: Bear : ?
questions.explanation: The peacock is India's national bird; the bear is Russia's national animal.

questions.stem: If the image of the letter 'A' is seen in a water reflection, how will it appear?
questions.explanation: A water reflection flips the figure top to bottom, so 'A' appears upside down. (The sheet shows a candidate chose 'completely reversed'.)

questions.stem: Circle : Sphere :: Square : ?
questions.explanation: A sphere is the 3D form of a circle; a cube is the 3D form of a square.

questions.stem: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than A but taller than B. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation: Order: C > A > D > B.

questions.stem: Five friends (A, B, C, D and E) are sitting in a straight line, all facing north. A is sitting to the immediate right of B. C is sitting to the immediate left of D. E is not sitting at any end. Who is sitting in the middle?
questions.explanation: The pairs (B,A) and (C,D) are each adjacent blocks, so the five seats are two blocks plus E. E cannot be at an end, so E is in the middle.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Axe, Dagger, Arrow, Knife
questions.explanation: Axe, dagger and knife are hand-held tools or weapons. An arrow is a projectile.

questions.stem: Arrange to make a coherent paragraph: A. It has offices at both Bangalore and Mumbai. B. Out of these, perhaps Goldman Sachs is the most well known in India. C. Some of the leading ones include Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers etc. D. There are many investment banks.
questions.explanation: D introduces the topic, C lists examples, B picks one ('Out of these'), A talks about it ('It').

questions.stem: Looking at a portrait of a man, Varun said, "His mother is the wife of my father's son. Brothers and sisters I have none." At whose portrait was Varun looking?
questions.explanation: With no siblings, 'my father's son' is Varun himself. His wife is the man's mother, so the man is Varun's son.

questions.stem: Arrange in dictionary order: 1. Read 2. Real 3. Ready 4. Rather 5. Ratify
questions.explanation: Rather, Ratify, Read, Ready, Real = 4, 5, 1, 3, 2.

questions.stem: Marathon is to Race as hibernation is to:
questions.explanation: A marathon is a type of race; hibernation is a type of (long) sleep.

questions.stem: A dice is rolled, and the top face shows 3. What number is on the bottom face?
questions.explanation: Opposite faces of a standard die add up to 7, so 7 - 3 = 4.

questions.stem: Arrange in dictionary order: 1. Telephone 2. Teleworker 3. Tendency 4. Temperature 5. Themselves
questions.explanation: Telephone, Teleworker, Temperature, Tendency, Themselves = 1, 2, 4, 3, 5.

questions.stem: Select the odd one out: Elephant, Cow, Lion, Hare
questions.explanation: Elephant, cow and hare are herbivores; the lion is a carnivore.

questions.stem: If in a certain language SPACE is coded as TQBDF, how will PURSE be coded?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves forward by 1: P-Q, U-V, R-S, S-T, E-F gives QVSTF.

questions.stem: What should a government employee do if they are offered a bribe?
options: Accept the bribe but report later
Refuse the bribe and report the incident immediately
Discuss the incident with colleagues first
questions.explanation: Offering or taking a bribe is an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The correct step is to refuse and report at once.

questions.stem: In India, the power to grant citizenship lies with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Citizenship is a Union subject. Under the Citizenship Act, 1955 it is granted by the Central Government, administered through the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.stem: India's first solar-powered village is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Modhera in Gujarat's Mehsana district was declared India's first 24x7 solar-powered village. Note that the sheet shows a candidate chose Rajasthan.

questions.stem: Which vitamin is also known as Ascorbic Acid?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.stem: The concept of 'Minimum Support Price' (MSP) is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: MSP is the price at which the government buys crops from farmers.

questions.stem: What is the significance of the 'e-Filing' system introduced under the e-Courts project?
options: It allows lawyers to file cases online
It totally eliminates physical presence during hearings
It restricts access to case records
It replaces judges with automated systems
questions.explanation: e-Filing lets advocates and litigants file petitions and documents online. It does not replace judges or remove hearings.

questions.stem: Which particle has a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons are negative. Protons are positive, neutrons neutral, and a positron is the positively charged antiparticle.

questions.stem: The first woman airline pilot was:
questions.explanation: Durga Banerjee became India's first woman commercial airline pilot in the 1950s. SCI later revised the answer key for this question, so check the final key.

questions.stem: The study of sound and sound waves is:
questions.explanation: Acoustics is the branch of physics dealing with sound. SCI revised the key for this question after objections.

questions.stem: 'Wake Up India' book was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Wake Up, India: A Plea for Social Reform' (1913) is by Annie Besant. (The sheet shows a candidate chose Lisa Ray.)

questions.stem: Which gas is responsible for the blue colour of the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The sky looks blue because N2 and O2 molecules scatter short (blue) wavelengths more (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.stem: Which country is famous for inventing the sandwich?
questions.explanation: The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich (England), 18th century.

questions.stem: Which two countries share the longest international border?
questions.explanation: The Canada-US border is the longest between two countries at about 8,900 km.

questions.stem: What is the highest-grossing animated movie of all time?
questions.explanation: Ne Zha 2 (2025) overtook Inside Out 2 to become the highest-grossing animated film. Time-sensitive: re-check if a newer film has passed it.

questions.stem: When do humans use more facial muscles?
questions.explanation: The popular claim is that frowning uses more muscles than smiling. The scientific evidence is weak, so this question is better learned as 'the key says frowning'.

questions.stem: What is the official currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: Yen. The won is South Korea's and the yuan is China's.

questions.stem: What is the name of the science that studies the past of life on earth?
questions.explanation: Palaeontology studies fossils and ancient life.

questions.stem: Pollen grains in plants are produced in:
questions.explanation: Pollen is produced in the anthers, which are part of the stamen (the male organ). 'Flower' is true but less precise.

questions.stem: Amnesty International has its headquarters at:
questions.explanation: Amnesty International is headquartered in London.

questions.stem: The Preamble to our Constitution includes all the following except:
questions.explanation: The Preamble mentions justice, liberty, equality of status and opportunity, and fraternity. 'Adult franchise' is in Article 326, not the Preamble.

questions.stem: Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Shendurney is in Kollam district, Kerala (Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve).

questions.stem: Which country has the highest life expectancy?
questions.explanation: Hong Kong tops this list at about 85 years, but rankings differ by year and source. SCI revised the key for this question, so check the final key.

questions.stem: What is acrophobia a fear of?
questions.explanation: Acrophobia = fear of heights.

questions.stem: What colours is the flag of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The UN flag is a white emblem on a light blue field.

questions.stem: What sporting event has a strict dress code of all-white?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is famous for its all-white dress rule.

questions.stem: OS stands for:
questions.explanation: OS = Operating System.

questions.stem: WINDOWS is a:
questions.explanation: Windows is Microsoft's operating system.

questions.stem: Video conferencing is the conduct of:
options: Video conference using a set of telescopic technology
questions.explanation: Video conferencing uses live audio-video links over telecom/internet.

questions.stem: Which of the following produces the best quality graphics reproduction?
questions.explanation: Plotters draw precise vector lines and are used for engineering drawings and large graphics.

questions.stem: Abacus was the first:
questions.explanation: The abacus is a manual (mechanical) calculating tool.

questions.stem: People often call ____ the brain of the computer system.
questions.explanation: The CPU is called the brain of the computer.

questions.stem: Whereas a computer mouse moves over the table surface, the trackball is:
questions.explanation: In a trackball the ball is rolled by hand while the device body stays still.

questions.stem: Programs such as Mozilla Firefox that serve as navigable windows into the Web are called:
questions.explanation: Firefox is a web browser.

questions.stem: What is the shortcut key for printing a document on a computer with Windows?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+P opens the Print dialog.

questions.stem: An error in a computer program is called:
questions.explanation: A bug is an error or flaw in software.

questions.stem: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: URL = Uniform Resource Locator.

questions.stem: Which type of software is used to surf the web?
questions.explanation: A web browser is used to browse websites.

questions.stem: Which key is used to delete the character to the left of the cursor?
questions.explanation: Backspace deletes to the left; Delete removes the character to the right.

questions.stem: What does the shortcut Ctrl + C do?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C = Copy; Ctrl+X = Cut; Ctrl+V = Paste.

questions.stem: What does LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: LAN = Local Area Network.

questions.stem: Which part of the computer is responsible for logical operations?
questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.stem: What does the acronym 'IP' in IP Address mean?
questions.explanation: IP = Internet Protocol.

questions.stem: Which shortcut is used for undo?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action.

questions.stem: Which shortcut is used to paste the selected text?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+V pastes.

questions.stem: How can you export a PowerPoint presentation as a PDF?
questions.explanation: In PowerPoint: File, then Export, then Create PDF/XPS Document.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a good practice for creating a strong password?
options: Using a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers and symbols
Using the same password for all accounts
questions.explanation: Strong passwords are long, mixed and unique to each account.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of cybercrime?
options: Hacking into someone's social media account
Writing code for a new application
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access to an account is a cybercrime (IT Act, 2000).

questions.stem: Monitor, printer and speakers are:
questions.explanation: They present results to the user, so they are output devices. (They are also hardware, and SCI revised the key here, so check the final key.)

questions.stem: Which application is commonly used to view PDFs?
questions.explanation: Adobe Acrobat Reader is the standard PDF viewer.

questions.stem: Microsoft Word is a software?
questions.explanation: Word is application software.
